title.title: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: for a nontrivial knot, different surgery slopes never give the same oriented 3-manifold

plain: Cut a knot out of space and glue the tube back with a twist: different twists always give different spaces

panels.axisLabel: surgery slope $r$ on a knot $K \subset S^3$

beats.text: Floer theory left one case: slopes $-2$ and $2$ on a genus-2 knot
A hypothetical homeomorphism gives a nonzero integer instanton count
Counted again on a monopole moduli space, it must vanish

steps: Earlier work left one suspect: slopes $+2$ and $-2$ on a genus-two knot
Suppose both gave the same space, and count instantons along the way
One count is nonzero, the other must vanish: impossible

achievement.label: Purely cosmetic surgery conjecture (Gordon 1990, Kirby problem 1.81)
achievement.context: Before: only $\pm 2$ on a genus-2 knot remained (Hanselman 2023; Daemi–Lidman–Miller Eismeier)
achievement.note: A 144-page monopole argument that gauge theorists have not yet checked

verify.detail: Manuscript only: the new part is a 144-page SO(3)-monopole cobordism argument
verify.ourCheck: We read the proof outline; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Cut out a knot, reglue it with a twist. Earlier work left one suspect pair.
Assume they match; one count comes out both nonzero and zero.
Claimed: different twists always give different spaces.
